items.title: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents typically append raw tool outputs to their context. Over multi-step interactions, long and noisy observations incur substantial context overhead and dilute the agent's attention to task-relevant information. Existing token pruning and summarization methods remain constrained by discrete text representations, limiting the achievable compression ratios. In this work, we challenge the prevailing assumption that agents must consume tool observations as explicit text tokens. To this end, we propose Coca-Cola, a continuous latent context compression model for LLM ag…

items.title: Signed but Steerable: Measuring and Closing the Text-Vector Integrity Gap in Offline Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary: Offline retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) on edge devices is updated through signed knowledge packs that carry text and precomputed embedding vectors. A signature proves who published a pack, not that its vectors encode its text. We study this text-vector integrity gap. A verifier that recomputes vectors and accepts them within a cosine tolerance concedes a predictable share of queries to an attacker who controls the vectors: the hijack rate equals the distribution of angular retrieval margins at the tolerance (the margin law). Margins are small in five corpora and two embedding models, so …

items.title: StepX-OPD: Rethinking Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation in Diffusion Models
items.summary: A deployable text-to-image diffusion model must hold several capabilities at once, such as instruction following, text rendering and human preference, and must sample in a few steps. Capabilities and few-step sampling are built in separate stages: a full-step model first consolidates capabilities through multi-teacher on-policy distillation, then serves as a fixed teacher for step distillation. Every full-step model we evaluate scores lower once compressed, and the second stage cannot begin until the first finishes. We introduce StepX-OPD, which merges the two stages: one student acquires ever…

items.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
items.summary: LLM-guided evolutionary search uses AI agents to improve programs for mathematical and computational problems by iteratively refining solutions and combining high-scoring methods. However, the process is often slow because the LLM generates a long textual chain of thought for each round and must repeat this generation many times to maintain population diversity. We present SwarmEvolve, a framework in which hundreds of low-cost agents per round work in swarms, reason in latent space without decoding to text, and share information by passing KV caches. Each swarm studies the problem from a diffe…

items.title: OpenFrontiers: A Collection of Open Research Problems and a Benchmark for Scientific Rediscovery
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have shown increasing promise in research-level problem solving, yet a comprehensive collection of such problems is still missing, and evaluating them on research-level problems remains challenging. We introduce OpenFrontiers, a cross-disciplinary resource that combines a structured corpus of open research problems with a retrospective benchmark of recently resolved problems in mathematics. The corpus records problem statements, context, progress, and other information for 12,151 problems. The benchmark contains 200 problems, 110 resolved in 2026 and 90 still open,…

items.title: Terminal-style Mathematical Modeling Bench: The First Agentic and Verifiable Benchmark for Mathematical Modeling
items.summary: Mathematical modeling turns an open-ended real-world problem into assumptions, a model, a solution, and a defended recommendation, and its answers matter only if they are both close to a credible reference and physically feasible; existing benchmarks either score solver fragments or grade reports with an LLM judge, leaving those numbers unchecked. We introduce TB-MathModel (the Terminal-style Mathematical Modeling Bench), the first benchmark to make complete contest-style modeling problems agentic, verifiable, and terminal at once, over 18 real CUMCM and MCM problems (2023--2025). Each task sh…

items.title: Muir: Linear Attention with Sensitivity-Allocated Gating and Matched-Filter Readout
items.summary: Linear attention compresses context into a fixed-size key-value state for linear-time training and constant-memory inference. Gated delta-rule models decay this state and erase its prediction for an incoming key before writing a new value; Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2) generalizes this with channel-wise decay and decoupled, full-rank erase and write gates. However, we show that state updates are far less sensitive to erasure than to writes: key activation and unit normalization concentrate key energy onto a sparse subset of channels, whereas value writes scale all channels, so the erase gate can be…

items.title: Information Games: Strategic Crowding and Firm Repositioning in Language-Model Space
items.summary: When firms respond to new market opportunities, their capacity choices alter the future discounted free cash flows available to both competitors and investors. In competitive markets, these investment decisions publicized in news articles and analyst reports, measuring the changes in capital structure, product mix, firm leadership, risk exposure and operating procedure made by the firm. Modern search engines rely on Large Language Models to measure the relevancy of source documents to given search query. These measurements let researchers represent these news articles as clouds of dense vector…

items.title: Reducing Representational Interference in Retrieval Embeddings with Trainable Prefix Tokens
items.summary: Embedding models compress variable-length text into fixed-size vector representations, but this compression can entangle semantic content with residual token-level information, such as artifacts arising from attention sink behavior. We propose a simple method that prepends trainable [DUMP] tokens to the input during embedding model training. The method keeps the model architecture, pooling strategy, and training loss unchanged, while optimizing the added tokens through the standard contrastive retrieval objective. By introducing trainable prefix positions that interact with regular tokens duri…

items.title: Hard Sample-Conditioned Decorrelated Attention for Robust Face Recognition
items.summary: Multi-head attention in Vision Transformers (ViTs) allows independent attention patterns across heads, but without explicit regularization, heads may learn redundant patterns rather than complementary roles. Correlation-based penalties encourage head disentanglement, yet apply uniform regularization across all training samples. In face recognition (FR), hard samples whose embeddings lie close to competing identities are critical for optimization and generalization. Motivated by this, we propose ViT-HarDis, which conditions attention head disentanglement on sample difficulty: samples with high …

items.title: On the Opportunities and Challenges of Prefill-to-Autoregressive Cross-Model Transfer
items.summary: Prefill-to-Autoregressive Cross-model Transfer (PACT), a form of latent communication between language models, combines a larger model's prompt representations with a smaller model's efficient generation, offering a promising way to balance capability and inference cost. However, existing systems provide limited support for independently evaluating large-small model collaboration, and improved task performance alone does not establish whether the receiver benefits from the sender's information. We introduce PLatour, an open-source PACT framework that connects frozen models through lightweight,…

items.title: Towards Real-Time Full-Waveform LiDAR Transformers via Intensity-Guided Token Reduction and Physics-Aware Augmentation
items.summary: LiDAR is a critical sensor for autonomous driving and robotics, yet it remains vulnerable to adverse conditions such as fog, rain, transparent objects, and low-reflectance surfaces. Full-waveform LiDAR (FWL) addresses these limitations by capturing the complete return waveform as a histogram, preserving rich reflection characteristics including multi-path echoes and weak signals. While recent Transformer-based approaches have demonstrated promise on FWL data, two fundamental bottlenecks remain: high computational cost from redundant tokens in low-intensity background regions, and limited gener…

items.title: SynthFaces: Balanced Large Scale Human Dataset
items.summary: The pursuit of fair and equitable AI in human-centric tasks is critically hindered by the inherent biases and privacy risks of real-world datasets, which offer imbalanced representations of identity and often contain sensitive personal information. Consequently, state-of-the-art generative models trained on this skewed data exhibit unfair performance, particularly in identity-preserving generation. In this work we propose a pipeline for controllable generation of dataset with diverse faces for generative models training and finetuning. We achieve this by expanding foundational Arc2Face diffusi…

items.title: Decoupled Predictive Decision Making: A Shared Conditional Predictor for Agents
items.summary: Agent decisions depend on empirical relationships that deployment observations reveal and task descriptions alone may leave unresolved. We introduce Decoupled Predictive Decision Making (DPDM), an architecture that formulates heterogeneous agent decisions as conditional prediction with a shared pretrained learner. Language models provide semantic representations of current and historical records, while a general-purpose conditional predictor predicts task-defined targets from the represented evidence. Pretraining supplies reusable inference capability; deployment evidence instantiates problem-…

items.title: SAE Interprets MoE: Sparse AutoEncoders Reveal That MoE Experts Exhibit Human-Interpretable Fine-Grained Specialization
items.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models route each token to a few of many experts, yet what an individual expert is responsible for remains unsettled. Existing analyses count how often an expert is selected on domain-labeled corpora, an instrument that fixes the taxonomy in advance, stays coarse, and records selection rather than contribution. We instead study specialization in feature space by training a sparse autoencoder (SAE) on the output of an MoE layer. items.title: HeLM: Hierarchical Explicit Language Memory for Non-Markovian Manipulation
items.summary: Recent advances in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have enabled fine manipulation capabilities, yet performing tasks that require working memory remains a key challenge. Most existing VLA architectures operate under a Markovian assumption, mapping only the current observation to an action, which leads to failure in non-Markovian environments. Inspired by the human 'inner monologue', we propose Hierarchical Explicit Language Memory (HeLM), a hierarchical VLA framework that maintains task-relevant history in explicit language through factorized event detection and event-triggered memory upda…

items.title: TailSteer: Trajectory-Tail Steering for Drift-Resistant Multi-turn Image Editing
items.summary: Strong single-turn editing performance does not guarantee reliable multi-turn interaction: as edited outputs are repeatedly reused, small unintended changes can accumulate into severe visual drift. This long-term drift is often mitigated through training on multi-turn data or cross-turn rollouts, potentially altering pretrained priors, or through specialized inference-time mechanisms that are difficult to scale to foundation models. We introduce TailSteer, a final-stage training framework that improves multi-turn robustness while retaining the generative and editing capabilities acquired throu…

items.title: From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts: Toward AI-Augmented Human Intelligence
items.summary: For a decade, progress in artificial intelligence has been measured by how much a machine can do on its own. Large foundation models now write code and run multistep tasks, and personal agents act on a person's behalf. Yet people still forget what they once knew, miss what they are not looking at, fail to find the right words, and face hard choices without the benefit of their own history, because the machine that could help stands outside the situation. As AI moves into the physical world, attention has settled on one kind of intelligent individual, the embodied robot; we argue that the era o…

items.title: EvoMemState: Evolving Memory State for Personal Agents
items.summary: Long-term memory enables large language model (LLM) agents to provide continuous personalized assistance by retaining user information across interactions. Existing systems support this process through fact extraction, organization, updating, and retrieval, but largely maintain memories as independent facts. This fact-centric paradigm may overlook how new facts update, constrain, or conflict with earlier ones, while leaving their applicability, role, and priority for the current request implicit. In this paper, we introduce EvoMemState, a state-centric framework that augments persistent facts …

items.title: Decode Before You Hear: Speculative Listening for Chunk-Interleaved Full-Duplex Speech Language Models
items.summary: Chunk-interleaved full-duplex speech language models listen and speak in fixed time chunks, and each chunk must be processed before the next one arrives. Their workload is asymmetric across chunks: listen chunks leave compute idle while awaiting audio, and speak and tool-call chunks require serial generation, which delays responses and tool calls. Using the idle compute for the next chunk requires decoding it before its audio arrives, under an assumed input. items.title: SLA: Scaling Spatial-Language-Action Model via Continual Pre-training
items.summary: Reliable robotic manipulation requires both semantic understanding and precise control in three-dimensional space. However, vision-language-action (VLA) foundations largely inherit visual representations from 2D vision-language pre-training, while spatial supervision is often introduced only during task-specific adaptation. Developing spatial understanding as a transferable foundation-model capability therefore calls for learning from broader robot experience. items.title: Future Representation Distillation for Imagination-free World Action Models
items.summary: World Action Models (WAMs) use the predictive knowledge of pretrained video diffusion models for robot control through future video prediction. However, iterative video denoising is costly, and inaccurate visual predictions can compromise action prediction. Our key idea is to make this predictive knowledge available through visual representations computed from the current observation, enabling action prediction without generating future videos. We introduce DreamFree, a WAM that repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a predictive visual encoder through representation distillation. Th…

items.title: Identically Trained Language Models Break on Different Jailbreaks
items.summary: Jailbreak benchmarks test one checkpoint and treat which jailbreaks break it as a property of its pretraining data and safety training. We ask whether another pretraining run of the same data, given the same safety training, would break on the same jailbreaks. For each of 25 pretraining data recipes, we take 1B base models from 3 pretraining seeds and give each the same safety post-training with 2 post-training seeds, for 150 models in all. items.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
items.summary: Models for physical AI tasks, such as robotics and autonomous driving, need not reason solely in language. They can use visual plans--points, bounding boxes, and trajectories--to represent spatial goals and anticipate motion. However, autoregressive vision-language models generate these plans one coordinate token at a time, making richer predictions increasingly costly. We introduce VFlash, a method for fast, accurate visual planning through Flash Primitive Decoding. items.title: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes
items.summary: User embeddings are central components of modern recommendation, personalization, and behavioral modeling systems. Though these embeddings can compactly encode rich behavioral information, they are inherently dense and opaque, limiting interpretability. To address this gap, we argue that user embeddings can be understood as sparse superpositions of interpretable behavioral modes. This structure is directly predicted by generative models of user behavior for linear embeddings and extends approximately to deep-learning representations by the superposition hypothesis. items.title: Do You Miss the Nights We Spent Crafting Figures? Rethinking Teaser and Framework Figures in the Age of Generative AI
items.summary: Scientific figures give research ideas a visual form through choices of abstraction, composition, and emphasis. Generative AI offers new ways to realize these choices, raising questions about explanatory clarity and purposeful visual expression. We examine these questions through a visual retrospective of 371 motivation and framework figures from 200 papers. The corpus comprises a quota-based main sample of 160 papers spanning four temporal periods and a separate purposive style-contrast sample of 40 papers. items.summary: Grounded reasoning, where a model outputs text coordinates of relevant locations in chain-of-thought reasoning, is a common strategy for solving complex visual reasoning problems. However, the benefits and limitations of grounded reasoning are understudied. We study where and why grounded reasoning is most useful. items.title: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists
items.summary: AI-Scientists arrived, but a world for them to grow in did not. Human scientists take theirs for granted $-$ centuries of open problems and shared ideas, waiting in the scientific literature. To AI-Scientists, that world is readable but not runnable, so we build Scientist World for them: every research paper becomes an executable environment. Our autonomous pipeline extracts each paper's open-ended research question and reproduces its proposed method as the baseline; an AI-Scientist entering the environment is evaluated against what the human authors achieved. items.title: EgoGeneralist: Unifying Egocentric Action-Video Tasks through Video-Native Modeling
items.summary: Modern video models possess strong visual priors, yet do not natively represent human action in metric 3D space. We present EgoGeneralist, which adapts pretrained video generators to unify action-conditioned egocentric video generation, pose estimation, and joint action-video generation. Our role-adaptive action renderer provides video-native representations for multidirectional action-video learning, making metric motion usable as both a spatial control signal and a recoverable generation target. items.title: XStack: A Benchmark for ML Repo Migration
items.summary: ML code should run where researchers choose, not where it was first written. Today, machine learning code mainly lives in two ecosystems, PyTorch on NVIDIA GPUs and JAX on Google TPUs. Migrating repositories between them means building and testing across frameworks and hardware. This migration is (1) a practical need, since it unlocks different hardware for researchers, and (2) a natural benchmark: it involves different frameworks and hardware, covers whole repositories, and is long-horizon and challenging. items.title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
items.summary: Interpretability, AI auditing and assessments of machine consciousness increasingly rest on mechanism-level quantities: functionals of a system's causal transition law that describe how it computes, not what it outputs. Experiments see that law only through finite, partial and noisy interventions. items.title: Towards interpreting any residual stream direction by scaling activation inversion
items.summary: To interpret a direction in a language model's residual stream, we can look for text that strongly activates it. But when such text is found by scanning a corpus, it is limited to what that corpus contains. We develop Maximally-Activating Example Metamodels (MAEMs), language models which map residual stream directions from a subject model to text exemplars that strongly activate those directions. Our objective is to maximise the cosine similarity of a supplied residual stream direction with the activations of the text generated by the MAEM. items.title: Adversarial Training with Large Step Sizes: Implicit Bias, Optimization, and Sharpness
items.summary: Adversarial Training (AT) is an important method for improving model robustness. We study the dynamics of deterministic Gradient Descent (GD) in AT. Most existing works in this direction focus on the small or vanishing step sizes regime, where GD resembles a continuous-time flow. However, such step sizes can make training inefficient and are rarely used in practice. In this paper, we study the AT dynamics of GD with large constant step sizes. We first study GD in adversarial linear logistic regression, focusing on two aspects: where the model parameters converge (implicit bias) and how quickly…

items.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own rollouts under a frozen teacher's per-token supervision. Does this dense signal reduce the training FLOPs needed to reach a target accuracy compared with reinforcement learning? We systematically compare vanilla reverse-KL OPD with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) across task difficulty, student and teacher size, domain, and optimization choices, measuring held-out accuracy against training FLOPs. items.title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
items.summary: Reproducing machine learning experiments requires reconstructing procedures from information scattered across papers, released code, and supporting artifacts. For coding agents, reproduction success can therefore depend on their ability to fill in missing details, rather than on the released artifacts alone. We ask whether preserving recovered procedures and decisions improves subsequent independent reproduction. items.summary: A defender anticipating an attacker needs a probability distribution over the attacker's next action from information available before that action occurs. Two structures complicate this: the attacker's behavioral regime persists and can switch within an episode, and each action combines an operation with state-dependent arguments whose feasible values change over time. We capture both with a hidden Markov model whose latent state is the active regime and whose regime-conditioned action law is defined on a feasibility-masked tree of executable actions. items.summary: Cyclist fatality rates remain high despite policy support for active travel, and autonomous vehicles add complexity to mixed traffic. Neither crash statistics nor multi-model detection pipelines scale to continuous monitoring of perceived safety along a route. items.title: 这大环境看来是很差了
items.summary: 前两天入职了一家公司，干的广州黄埔某国企外包深圳融创项目，新入职的一共几个人。早上开完会，下午去现场，这边一个叶姓领导去联系那边领路开门。 / 到了门口等了十几分钟门没开，电话里问他到底联系对地方没有、确认下情况，结果这哥们张嘴就 TMTM 地说话。 / 我反驳了几句，让他就事论事，不要拿情绪说话。我才第一天进来，就见过一眼，这哥们就搁那儿喷。我翻开他的钉钉职位一看，副经理。难怪对第一面、第一天入职的人都这么横。果不其然，第二天就被穿小鞋公报私仇了，说什么“不符合试用期录用标准”。合着第一面、第一天，能忍受得了对父母问候，才是你们公司的企业文化考核是吧？还问我到底懂没懂，这哥们自己没懂别人想表达啥，还觉得自己有道理。 / 这哥们也能当经理、还能做到这个位置，应该是历史遗留产物了。学历背景我不评价，但沟通素质确实拉胯，对素不相识、第一天入职的人直接爆粗口，这管理水平我是不敢恭维。 / 说起来其他入职的几个哥们也是人才，短期项目、没有正儿八经的合同都要去做，都是五六年经验的人了，这行情这么差么？我了解到的情况是短期项目、合同和社保情况都不太清晰。这家公司叫铭思，Boss 上写的是 14-16 ，结果面过了又是另一个价格，还是短期项目，然后还说自己不知情，到底知不知情我就不知道了。有时间的可以去 Boss 搜索，现在还挂着呢。 / 说这么多也不是完全为了泄愤。收到消息的时候，我完全觉得很…

items.title: 写了个开源工具：手机照片视频无损搬到电脑，局域网直传， PC 不装任何客户端
items.summary: 写了个工具解决自己的痛点，开源出来给大家用，求轻喷、求反馈。 **GitHub**： https://github.com/malatomato1989/photosmove **官网**： **Google Play**：搜索 PhotosMove ，或 ### 起因 老婆手机里攒了 1600+ 张照片、20 多个 G 的视频，想搬进电脑做本地备份，把主流方案试了一圈，都有点膈应： - **微信/QQ 传文件助手**：图片走压缩管道，视频超过 1GB 直接传不了，传完时间戳和 EXIF 还可能被动过 - **网盘**：上传即转码的风险 + 不开会员限速，几十 G 要传到天荒地老，而且照片这东西我不想让它过第三方服务器 - **数据线 MTP**：能保证原样，但大批量传的时候慢、偶发中断，中途断了还得从头排查哪些传了哪些没传 - **LocalSend / Syncthing**：好用，但电脑端要装客户端，用起来有点不顺手 我的需求其实很简单朴素：**手机里的照片视频原封不动落到电脑上，电脑端一个浏览器就能搞定**。找不到完全对口的，就自己写了一个。 ### 用法 1. 手机装 PhotosMove （ Google Play ），点一下启动服务 2. 电脑浏览器打开手机上显示的地址，输 6 位 PIN 码 3. 勾选相册 → 浏览器开始下载一个流式 ZIP ，完事 PC 端零安装…

FinalShell 开源了？类 FinalShell 的 SSH 客户端 —— FinallyShell
items.summary: 相信这里很多人都用过 FinalShell ，我自己也很喜欢，一直觉得它是最顺手的 ssh 工具。不过现在是 2026 年了，客户端还是 Java 写的，Mac 上的体验也一直挺差... 趁周末 token 重置之前，我用 Opus 5.5 神力对着 FinalShell 复刻了一个出来，换了 go 来写，UI 用的是最近中文推上挺火的 MyGo UI： 项目地址： https://github.com/TooonyChen/finallyshell/ https://i.imgur.com/bt7jS7t.png https://i.imgur.com/LHp9Lyw.png https://i.imgur.com/2rdiEd8.png 布局基本照着 FinalShell 做的，只不过改了一个左边竖排会话标签出来（我不喜欢横向 tab ）。 老用户打开就能上手。基本功能都齐活了： - 能直接导入 FinalShell 的连接和分组（密码导不过来，要重新输一遍） - 终端内核用 Ghostty 的 libghostty-vt ，配色直接用 Ghostty 默认，可以设背景图 - 自带编辑器，有语法高亮、多光标、查找替换，GBK / GB18030 的文件打开不乱码 - 服务器监控：CPU 、内存、负载、网络、延迟、磁盘、进程，两秒刷新一次 - SFTP 拖拽上传，三个任务并发，失…
